title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is isolated. The neighbouring scans are typed pages of an unrelated text on p-adic holomorphic functions (Serre/Bourbaki style). It is a sketch titled 'Dé-trivialisation de ξ_p ?'.

Setting, as far as it can be read:
- 𝒪 is a set of 'orders' o. Context strongly suggests maximal orders in the definite quaternion algebra B_{p,∞}, i.e. endomorphism rings of supersingular elliptic curves.
- The objects are pairs (M,o): M is an F-crystal of rank 2 over F_{p^2} or over F̄_p, with an action of o. Concretely this is the Dieudonné crystal of a supersingular elliptic curve with its endomorphism action. Since o⊗Z_p is the maximal order of the local quaternion division algebra, M is of supersingular type.
- 𝒯_p is the set of 'functions' ξ assigning to each (M,o) a class u_ξ(M,o) in Isom(Λ²M, T_p)/Z_p^{*2}. Here T_p is the Tate crystal. This is a crystalline analogue of choosing an orientation of det T_ℓ(E) ≅ Z_ℓ(1), the Weil-pairing side.
- Quotienting by Z_p^{*2} is exactly right. Automorphisms of (M,o) commute with o⊗Z_p = O_D, so they are central, i.e. scalars λ∈Z_p^*. These act on Λ²M by λ². Only the class mod squares is therefore well defined on isomorphism classes.

The axioms:
- (i) Invariance under isomorphisms (M,o)→(M',o').
- (ii) Compatibility with the Serre tensor construction. Take an invertible right-projective rank-1 o-module (a bimodule) P, and o' = End_o(P). Then M' = P⊗_o M is again such an object. One has det M' ≅ (N_{o/Z}P)⊗det M ≅ det M, using the canonical trivialisation N_{o/Z}(P) ≅ Z given by the reduced norm of an ideal. The triangle det M → det M' → T_p must commute. In modern terms: the orientations are compatible along the Deuring correspondence (connecting ideals ↔ isogenies).

The NB reads (ii) 'strictly'. One is given orders o, o', bimodules _oP_{o'}, and isomorphisms P⊗Z_p ≅ Hom_cris(M,M'). Under that reading, (i) becomes equivalent to Galois stability: invariance under isomorphisms k̄→k̄', i.e. under the Frobenius of k̄ (or of F_{p^2}).

So 𝒯_p is a torsor of compatible 'p-adic orientations' of the supersingular isogeny category. The title asks whether a canonical element ξ_p, apparently a trivialisation coming from elsewhere (ℓ-adic/adelic or motivic data), can be 'de-trivialised', i.e. is non-canonical, or how it twists.

This fits a Galois-theory-of-motives programme. The idea is to describe the fibre functor / gerbe of motives over finite fields generated by supersingular elliptic curves, using quaternion orders and their ideal bimodules plus a p-adic crystalline component. That is close in spirit to the later Langlands–Rapoport / Milne description of the motivic gerbe over F_p in terms of Weil numbers and its local components at p.
errors: The text is a sketch and the final question is not resolved; ξ_p itself is never defined on this page.

Writing N_{o/Z}(P) ≅ Z presupposes P is a locally free ideal with reduced norm 1 after identification, or a choice of positive generator. For general invertible bimodules the reduced norm is a positive rational / an ideal of Z, and the identification with Z uses positivity. This is implicit.

Over F_{p^2}, as opposed to F̄_p, not every supersingular Dieudonné module has all endomorphisms defined. The 'F_{p^2} (ou F̄_p)' alternative glosses over the descent issue, which the NB then partly addresses via Frobenius stability.
The archive dating '1965' is hard to reconcile with the language of F-cristaux and the Tate crystal. That vocabulary suggests ≥1968–70, consistent with the 'vers 1977' typescript layer.

ideas.what: Supersingular elliptic curves / their F-crystals with an action of a maximal quaternion order, related by invertible bimodules P via M' = P⊗_o M
ideas.modern_name: Deuring correspondence; Serre tensor construction; Morita equivalence of maximal orders (connecting ideals)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941), Serre tensor construction (Serre, 1960s), Waterhouse (1969), Ribet/Gross for ideal-isogeny dictionary

ideas.what: Determinant of rank-2 F-crystal identified with Tate crystal; orientation classes modulo Z_p^{*2}, compatible with det(P⊗M) ≅ N(P)⊗det M
ideas.modern_name: crystalline Weil pairing / orientation of supersingular Dieudonné modules; reduced norm compatibility
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Oda, Mazur–Messing for crystalline Weil pairing)

ideas.what: Equivalence between functoriality under the bimodule/isogeny category and Galois (Frobenius) stability under isomorphisms of algebraically closed fields
ideas.modern_name: descent of p-adic component of the motivic gerbe / Langlands–Rapoport style description of supersingular isogeny classes

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a torsor 𝒯_p of compatible crystalline orientations on the category of supersingular F-crystals with quaternion-order action. He asks whether a given trivialisation ξ_p can be 'de-trivialised'. This looks like a step toward describing the p-component of the motivic Galois gerbe over finite fields via quaternion orders, anticipating the Langlands–Rapoport/Milne pseudo-motivic groupoid. The thread is left open.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it would document Grothendieck working on the structure of the motivic gerbe at p for supersingular motives with explicit crystalline data, before Langlands–Rapoport. Mathematically the content is now subsumed by known theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an interesting, isolated glimpse of Grothendieck combining F-crystals, quaternion orders, connecting bimodules and Tate-crystal orientations, in a 'Galois theory of motives' context. However, it is a fragmentary sketch whose content is now standard (Deuring, Serre tensor construction, Langlands–Rapoport). The novelty is mainly historical.

'associe une classe' — the struck word before 'classe' appears to be 'isom' (crossed out); the value is u_ξ(M,o) ∈ Isom(Λ²M, T_p)/Z_p^{*2}, with 'cristal de Tate' written under T_p.
(ii): reads roughly 'Pour (M,o) et P un o-module inversible à droite projectif de rg 1'.
'si o' = End_o(P)' is inserted above, replacing the struck 'est son commutant'.
'et on a alors un isomorphisme canonique de F-cristaux' (the line below P⊗_o M); the symbol is N_{o/Z} (reduced norm), first written as A then overwritten N.
The diagram has det(M) →~ det M' with both diagonal arrows u_ξ(M,o), u_ξ(M',o') marked '~' into T_p.
